note: Blocker round zblk (SOCCER first_to_score_event#archetype_mismatch): remove stale Method interactions from FTTS, attach the two inputs its stage s3 uses, and carry the inputs the knockout and winner records reference. soc.winning_margin_distribution stays retired (audited DUPLICATE of soc.goal_dist).

attach.why: FTTS settles over the entire game including extra time, so stage s3 and the interaction with soc.dixon_coles_low_score need the extra-time goal rate for the 91-120 part of the race window.
In second legs the aggregate decides which side attacks from kickoff; stage s3 and the interaction with soc.knockout_cagey_factor use it to shift the first-goal hazard and the no-goal mass.

In FTTS it only scales both teams' hazards in cup knockouts and second legs, moving the goalless leg and the race window; irrelevant to league and neutral-final series, so secondary context rather than a primary driver.
Kickoff heat, humidity and altitude (Liga MX, AFC and some qualifier venues) can lower both intensities and the early-goal hazard; used in stage s1 as a context multiplier.
The no-goal leg is the joint 0-0 cell of the goal-count model, so carrying it ties FTTS to the same model as the sibling match-result, totals and BTTS prices (stage s2).
In a second leg the aggregate, not the match score, must be level for extra time and it sets each team's risk posture; used in stage s6 and the tie-tree interaction.

Stage s6 composes advancement for non-final, two-leg and straight-to-penalties ties from the competition rule table, reading the aggregate state from soc.second_leg_aggregate_state instead of re-estimating it.
Joint goal-count model that owns the score grid: the level-after-90 probability is its diagonal (stages s1, s2) and it supplies the signed margin for the conditional league MOV stage s7.

unreg:knockout_method_of_victory.mechanism: A knockout tie decided in one match (a final, a single-leg cup tie, or the deciding match after an aggregate) is resolved in one of three ordered phases. Regulation (90 minutes plus stoppage) ends the tie when the score is unequal; otherwise 30 minutes of extra time are played, and a level score after 120 minutes goes to a penalty shootout. Method of Finish asks which phase ends the tie; Method of Victory asks which phase a named team wins in. The probability mass is generated by the regulation-draw probability (driven by the strength gap, the low total goal rate typical of finals and late risk aversion), the extra-time scoring rate under fatigue and extra substitutions, and a near-coin-flip shootout.

attach.why: Stage s8 residuals without rules text (KXAFCCL2GAME, KXWCWINMARGIN if it is a match margin, the third-place match) are priced from the joint goal-count distribution; it replaces the retired duplicate soc.winning_margin_distribution.
